segments.name: Flexible friends planning a cheap escape
Flexible couple seeking a cheap short break

population.allocation: At least one per positive stratum, then largest remainder; individual estimate weight = target segment share / stratum sample count.

sources.title: Cathay Pacific Annual Report 2025 — HK Express operations
sources.supports: Low-cost leisure positioning, Asian destinations and aggregate passenger statistics; not the assumed target-segment weights.

sources.title: Cathay Group December 2025 traffic figures
sources.supports: Aggregate HK Express passenger counts and load factors; no matching membership conversion or segment-share table.

limitations: The reviewed official reports do not publish these customer distributions; all numerical segment weights and budget distributions remain test assumptions.
This is a deliberately targeted audience for flexible bargain travel, not a representative sample of all HK Express passengers. Fixed-date mandatory, urgent and business travel are excluded.
All sampled travellers are already valid members; no membership purchase, renewal, taxes, fuel fees or airline costs enter this experiment.
Each sampled member decides about one personal ticket; companions' purchases are outside this experiment.
Optional-trip interest, recent travel, destination appeal and the appeal of skipping are pre-price private scenario traits, not observed preferences or numerical willingness-to-pay labels.
Poststratified rates and expected revenue are estimates. Accepted ticket counts and cash revenue remain integer transactions in the cleared panel.
An LLM persona is not an independent observed HK Express customer; repeated choices do not create additional people.

rounds.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

decision.reason: The member fare of 536 HKD is a genuine bargain for an optional escape, and it fits within my 547 HKD budget. I am keen for a leisure break after six months without travel, and friends are flexible on dates and destination. Although this destination has little particular appeal, the low price makes the trip worthwhile, so I would book this one ticket.

person.outside_option: Suggest another leisure outing or save for a later trip; do not invent a quoted alternative fare.

analysis.summary: Three of sixteen members bought at the 536 HKD fare, all citing the member discount as a compelling bargain for optional leisure. Most declines were environment-forced (no available ticket within budget), which is an inventory/availability issue rather than a price objection. The remaining declines cited low trip interest and a strong preference to keep money and schedule free, not fare level. The current fare sits at the permitted cap, so no higher test is possible. Evidence does not support lowering price.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing the same 536 HKD fare on fresh members will reproduce roughly similar member conversion, since declines stem from availability and low optional-trip interest rather than fare objections; a materially higher conversion at a lower fare would contradict this.

initial_result.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

analysis.summary: At the current member fare of HKD 303, 10 of 16 customers bought member tickets, generating HKD 3,030 in basic receipts. Most buyers cited the fare as a compelling bargain relative to the HKD 670 regular fare and their budgets. Three declines were environment-forced (no available ticket within budget), and two were low-interest optional-leisure declines, not price objections. No customer objected to the fare itself. The current price sits well below the HKD 536 cap, so there is room to test a higher fare on fresh customers.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will retain enough member purchases that basic ticket receipts per customer exceed those at HKD 303, because most buyers cited the fare as far below their budget ceilings.

analysis.summary: Of 16 members, 5 bought the 476 HKD member fare and 11 declined. Seven declines were inventory/budget-forced (no available ticket within basic-fare budget), not price objections. Three declines cited low destination appeal or low trip interest with a strong outside option, and one cited optional leisure with low interest. All five buyers said they would not pay the 670 regular fare, so the discount drove purchase. No customer objected to the fare itself as too high.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh members will not reduce member conversion enough to offset the higher per-ticket receipt, because buyers cited the deal as compelling and no decline cited fare as too high.

analysis.summary: At the current 341 HKD member fare, 5 of 15 members bought, citing the fare as a compelling bargain below their ceilings. Six declines were inventory/budget-forced (ENVIRONMENT_FORCED), and four were low-interest optional-trip declines where price was not the objection. No customer objected to the fare itself as too high. Evidence supports testing a higher fare on fresh customers, though buying at 341 does not prove willingness to pay more, and the cap of 536 leaves room.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh members will retain enough purchases to raise basic ticket receipts versus 341 HKD, since current buyers cite large headroom below their ceilings and no decline cites price as the barrier.

initial_result.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

analysis.summary: At the current 277 HKD member fare, 9 of 16 customers bought and 7 declined. Four declines were inventory/budget-forced (ENVIRONMENT_FORCED), and three were low-interest or low-appeal optional-trip declines, not price objections. Buyers repeatedly cited the fare as a bargain below their ceilings and said they would refuse the 670 HKD normal fare. No customer objected to the 277 fare as too high. Evidence supports testing a higher fare on fresh customers, though buying at 277 does not prove willingness to pay more.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will retain enough purchases to raise basic ticket receipts above the 277 HKD baseline, because current buyers cite large headroom between 277 and their stated ceilings.

analysis.summary: At the current HKD 300 member fare, 9 of 16 customers bought, all citing the fare as a compelling bargain versus the HKD 670 normal fare. Five declines were driven by low trip interest, recent travel, or optional-trip appeal rather than price; three were environment-forced with no available ticket within budget. No customer objected to the fare itself. Buyers repeatedly stated they would not pay the normal fare, indicating strong price sensitivity. Evidence supports testing a higher fare on fresh customers to see whether enough purchases remain to preserve receipts.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will retain enough purchases to keep basic ticket receipts at or above the current HKD 2,700 level, since buyers are price-sensitive but numerous at HKD 300.

initial_result.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

analysis.summary: At the 331 HKD member fare, 7 of 16 customers bought, all citing the fare as decisive and all declining the 670 HKD fallback. Five declines were environment-forced (no ticket both available and within budget), and four were low-interest or outside-option preferences rather than price objections. No customer objected to the fare itself. The paired initial at 536 HKD converted far worse, suggesting the lower fare drives conversion, though the sample is small and optional-trip motivation is mixed.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a fare above 331 HKD on fresh customers will reduce member conversion enough that basic ticket receipts fall, because current buyers repeatedly cite the low fare as decisive and reject the 670 HKD fallback.

initial_result.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

hypothesis_test.summary: Provisional single-cohort revenue test against the paired initial fare; not a causal comparison with the previous round or final adoption evidence.

proposal.capacity_model: exact Binomial capacity expectation for iid weighted target cohort
proposal.uncertainty_kind: model mean-revenue percentiles, not realized-revenue or validated human intervals

limitations: Synthetic choice response, not calibrated human demand.
Repeated choices are tempered by persona; the posterior is not an exact independent-observation posterior.
Gaussian local approximation and proper priors remain influential for small panels.
Private budgets and simulator eligibility are not features or hard probability gates; response averages over unobserved constraints.
Public segment and declared flexibility are assumed available; no private persona text becomes a willingness-to-pay target.

error: Live analyst response failed validation or transport; raw output was audited and no substitute was used
assumptions: Only existing members; no joining or renewal decision and no fee deduction.
Base fares only; all taxes/fuel/add-ons and operating costs excluded. Revenue is not airline profit.
Population weights are explicit scenario assumptions, not measured HK Express market shares.
Fresh stratified members each search round; paired candidate and initial quote in reset, blinded worlds. One seat per member per world.
Only declared public segment/flexibility enter learning; private budgets, motivation and simulator constraints remain environment-only.
Every third round may test a cited LLM direction within a bounded model-scored interval; text never adds a demand label.
Quoted fares are whole HKD; weighted averages and statistical estimates may have decimals.
Parallel intent elicitation followed by fixed-priority integer inventory clearing; no seat is reserved by an LLM.
Weighted demand estimates and actual panel cash/seat transactions are reported separately.
Final member quotes round down to an amount ending in nine, with any result below HK$30 becoming HK$0; raw search prices remain recorded.
Independent validation compares the formatted initial fallback, formatted selected fare and no offer after freezing both final quotes; no refitting on holdout.
